title: lullwatch field annotations
content:
Purpose: compact, very-local notes for the Lullwatch rotation (3am-7am) — not an org runbook, just the fast map I use when I wake up. Keep this small, writable, and invalidatable when infra changes.

Top-of-shift checklist (first 5 minutes):
- Slack: join #lullwatch (pin channel) and glance at pinned incidents
- Pager: check missed alerts in PagerDuty; ack any ongoing (only ACK if you're taking it)
- Dashboard quick glance: routing-latency p90 > 300ms? service-errors spike?
- Tail the proxy logs for 10s: sudo journalctl -u redwood-proxy -n 200 -f

Quick diagnostics primer (order matters):
1) Is the issue global or single-customer? (check alert title + /observability/requests route)
2) Check GPU hosts for pressure: ssh node-gpu-01; run nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
   - if memory% > 90% and many processes, suspect runaway KV cache or unbounded batch.
3) Serving runtime health: curl -sS http://localhost:8080/health || journalctl -u serving-runtime -n 200 --no-pager
4) Queue depth: curl localhost:9200/metrics | grep open_requests (if > 200, scale/pause traffic)

Common recovery playbooks (fast, testable):
- Model OOM / OOM-killer: 
  1. Graceful route drain: /api/admin/drain-route?route=<route-id> (returns 202)
  2. Scale down batch_size via feature flag (console -> route -> override) to 1
  3. If node in OOM state, isolate: ./scripts/mark-host-maintenance node-gpu-XX
  4. Restart serving runtime: sudo systemctl restart serving-runtime (watch logs)

- Latency spikes from prefix cache misses:
  1. Check cache hit-rate: /observability/cache/hit-rate?model=<id>
  2. If hit-rate < 10% and load is steady, temporarily enable prefix-caching-disabled=false for the route
  3. Roll back within 10–15m if errors increase

- High request 5xxs after deploy:
  - Roll to previous model variant: POST /api/models/<model>/rollout with body {"percent":0}
  - If rollout API fails, toggle traffic to fallback region via routing policy in Console (region: us-west-2 fallback).

Emergency commands I keep memorized:
- sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime -f --since "5m"
- kubectl get pods -n redwood --selector=app=serving-runtime -o wide
- ssh jump && ./bin/pool-status --summary
- curl -XPOST "https://infra-svc/internal/evacuate?host=node-gpu-03"

Escalation contacts (fast):
- On-call infra lead: Luis Ortega (Pager + Slack DMs)
- Serving runtime owner: Priya Desai (Slack: @priya, phone on PD)
- SRE rotational backup: eng-sre-rotation@redwood.com

Notes-to-self / heuristics:
- If error rate climbs but CPU/GPU look idle, check for staging traffic leak (common: misrouted proxy rule)
- Don’t restart redis-primary unless you confirm persistence is healthy; otherwise run redis-check AOF first
- If invoking rollback, annotate the incident with the exact model and container id (helps the model team)

Short-term TODO (for next lullwatch):
- Add a single-command helper that prints: open_requests, free_gpu_mem, recent_rollouts (idea: ./lullwatch-status)
- Confirm the new autoscaler ramp policy in dev cluster mirrors prod before enabling in prod
- Propose a small playbook for cache warming during traffic surges (draft in INF-412)

Open questions / unresolved:
- What’s the current safe memory margin for 16GB GPUs after quantization changes? (ask Applied ML team)
- Can we expose an aggregated short-id in alerts (model:variant@route) instead of long UUIDs?

Sign-off: if you’re taking the shift, reply in this doc with time + quick note (e.g., "Samira in: 03:12 — looked at proxy, nothing else urgent").

Appendix: quick snippet I paste into Slack for resets:
> Re-routing a route to fallback region (us-west-2):
> 1) Console -> Routes -> <route> -> Edit routing policy -> add fallback region us-west-2 (weight 100)
> 2) Monitor p50/p95 for 5m, then if stable remove fallback

End of notes.
